cultural.vision_reason: This is a documentary photograph of a man in traditional dress (feather headdress, fur skirt, animal-tail ornaments, shield and spear) associated with "Frank Fillis's Savage South Africa" exhibition; the attire is broadly consistent with southern African Nguni-type costume, though "Prince Lobengula" is actually a Ndebele/Matabele royal name, making the ethnic attribution plausible for the region. It is a photo, not a painting-mss.

physical.title: photographic print
physical.summary:
South Africa, full length frontal portrait of Ndebele "Prince Lobengula" standing outdoors. Wearing costume including skirt of striped animal tails, fur ankle-ornaments and wrist-ornaments, feather arm-ornaments, cape and head-dress. Holding animal-hide shield in one hand, spear in other. Section-view of European building in background.
Medium: Gelatin silver print.
Format: Print mounted on card.
